Ana Ruiz (support): Hey team — escalating a live customer issue (ACME, ticket #45789). They call /v1/embeddings with model 'text-embedding-small-768' and are getting vectors of length 1536. They pasted the exact curl they used below, might be an auth/header routing problem.

Acme Data Team: here's our request (redacted keys):
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer proj_ABC123" \
  -H "X-Org: org-ACME" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"text-embedding-small-768","input":["accounting record"]}'
```

Ana Ruiz (support): They do include both the project token and the org header. Customer expectation: 768-dim vectors. Actual: 1536-dim vectors. Customer sees no errors, just wrong shape. They also reported throughput degradation compared to their previous tests.

TJ Park (eng): I pulled proxy logs for their request id. Routing shows: 
```
[2026-03-14T10:07:03Z] request_id=rcq-9f8a auth.project=proj_ABC123 auth.org=org-ACME model_param=text-embedding-small-768 -> routed_model=rwd-embed-v2-1536 reason=org_default_priority
```
It looks like the router matched an org-level default embed model and chose that rather than honoring the requested model alias. This lines up with the 1536 dim output.

Jiang Li (ml-infra): This smells like the change from PR #2123 where we added org-level default model selection. There was a subtlety: router precedence changed so when an org header is present we consult org catalog first. If the org has an alias that resolves to a different canonical model (e.g., 'text-embedding-small' -> 'rwd-embed-v2-1536' for their SSO org), we override. We didn't break on explicit canonical model ids, only aliases. If customer used an alias that collides with an org alias, it can get mapped incorrectly.

TJ Park (eng): Repro steps I used locally:
1) Use a project-scoped token (proj_...) with no X-Org header -> request goes to project catalog -> returns 768d model.
2) Add X-Org: org-ACME -> router consults org catalog -> returns org default 1536d.

Workarounds for support to give customer right now:
- Ask them to send the canonical model id (non-ambiguous) instead of alias, e.g. 'text-embedding-small-768-v2' if available.
- Or include an explicit X-Project header to force project-scoped routing: 
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer proj_ABC123" \
  -H "X-Project: proj_ABC123" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"text-embedding-small-768","input":["accounting record"]}'
```
Either workaround causes router to pick the expected 768-dim model in my tests.

Jiang Li (ml-infra): Long term fix: revert precedence so explicit model param (canonical or alias) and project mapping take precedence over org default unless org is explicitly opting in to override models (we never fully rolled that out). I'm preparing a small patch to router selection logic + unit tests. Patch: infra/router#patch-3345.

ops-bot: deploy plan attached: PATCH infra/router#3345 -> canary deploy to us-east-1 tomorrow 2026-03-15 02:00 UTC, full roll 2026-03-15 06:00 UTC. No schema changes.

Ana Ruiz (support): Communicated workaround to ACME and escalated for an urgent patch. Customer asked about billing: will they be charged differently for 1536 vs 768 throughput? Accounting says usage is per-token, but model unit cost differs; ops to review billing adjustments if they incurred outsized cost.

TJ Park (eng): I verified a minimal regression test: when Authorization=proj and X-Org present, explicit canonical model id wins, alias resolution now respects project mapping after patch. Patch PR: https://git.redwood.ai/infra/router/pulls/3345 (description: prefer explicit model param > project catalog > org-default).

support-bot: ACME updated and replied: "After adding X-Project header and switching to canonical id our vectors are 768 and similarity baseline OK. Thanks." :white_check_mark:

Ana Ruiz (support): Customer confirmed throughput normalized and vector dims corrected. Will keep ticket open until canary completes.

Jiang Li (ml-infra): Ops note: audit log shows ~12 requests from the customer during window that got 1536 vectors; will run a one-off billing review.

Ana Ruiz (support): Closing loop here for now — handing to TJ/Jiang to monitor canary and billing. Thanks team. :thumbsup:
